newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CNB calls for body salvaging troubled banks. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czech CNB calls for body salvaging troubled banks. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) has proposed creation of a state-run body which would buy doubtfull credit from banks in order to prevent their failure.

A CNB report to the parliament obtained by Reuters on Tuesday said another institution should take stakes in endangered banks if there was no interest to do so among private investors. (Corrects to make clear the CNB wants to create two separate institutions)
"The CNB has prepared a model of a centralised solution of the problems of bad loans with the possibility of a state support," the report said.
It added that the organisation could be set up by the CNB, the Finance Ministry and possibly by the International Finance Corporation, the investment arm of the World Bank.
"So far the talks with the existing state institutions (Konsolidacni Banka, Ceska Inkasni Jednotka) (on taking such a role) have not led to success," the report said.

The material, reviewing the central bank forced administration of 12 local banks in recent years, was released by the CNB ahead of the Governor Josef Tosovsky's testimony on the state of the banking sector to parliament on Tuesday.

The report said that the state will have spent about 90 billion crowns in cleaning up the post-Communist books at Czech banks, and that the banking sector overall was sound after two periods of consolidation.

The report also called for the creation of an umbrella market watchdog with extensive authorities which would oversee the work of regulators on the banking, insurance and capital markets. -- Jan Lopatka, Prague Newsroom, 42-2-2423-0003
